elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly states that “Corio may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience right is exercisable during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The right is not limited to a term end and therefore applies during the five-year initial term and renewal terms.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “thirty (30) days' prior” notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires “prior written notice.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees following Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Commerce One must refund “any prepaid fees” allocable to the period after the effective termination date, which operationally provides a pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: No clause grants Commerce One a mid-term convenience right. Section 11.1 permits nonrenewal only at the expiration of a term, while Section 11.2 concerns cause-based termination.

elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate the Agreement for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Corio receives an unrestricted convenience-termination right that is not limited to a term end.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period is at least 60 days and no more than 90 days.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is 30 days, outside the specified 60–90-day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The clause prohibits any penalty, early-termination fee, or other charge, so the applicable fee is zero and does not exceed the cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only effective at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Commerce One has no mid-term convenience right; its only convenience-like right is Section 11.1 nonrenewal at expiration of the initial or renewal term.

elements.element: Vendor must provide 90 days' notice to terminate for convenience at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 requires only 30 days' prior notification from either party, not 90 days.

result.reason: The operative convenience-termination paragraph fully meets the preferred position: Corio can terminate during the committed term on 30 days' written notice, receives a refund of prepaid post-termination fees, and Commerce One has no mid-term convenience right. The fallback is not independently satisfied because Customer's notice period is 30 rather than 60–90 days and Vendor's term-end notice requirement is 30 rather than 90 days. The redline is not minimal because it also adds an extensive Section 11.3 containing unrelated survival, ongoing-access, support, payment, and confidentiality provisions. Those provisions create tension with a complete convenience exit and the promise of no other charge because existing-customer payment obligations survive any termination. Drafting is otherwise serviceable but includes an unnumbered convenience provision, “it's” instead of “its,” and inherited malformed hyphenation.
